description: Verify that ARP cache entries age out even when in active use — DUT must re-ARP after the timeout despite ongoing UDP traffic to the same IP, so peers see fresh resolution attempts on a regular schedule
approach:
[Objective]
Stricter than ARP_48: even if the entry is being used, DUT must still re-resolve once <DYNAMIC-ARP-CACHE-TIMEOUT> seconds have passed since the last *learning* event. Continuous traffic does not refresh the timer; only fresh ARP responses do.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected → DUT learns <HOST-1-IP, MAC-ADDR1>.

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup → DUT sends UDP #1 (eth_dst=MAC-ADDR1).

3. Active wait of <DYNAMIC-ARP-CACHE-TIMEOUT> seconds with the tester continuing to keep the entry 'in use' (e.g. periodic traffic). The entry must still age.

4. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup again → DUT sends UDP #2 (eth_dst=MAC-ADDR1, still using cache).

5. Observation: at some point during/after step 3, DUT must emit its own ARP Request for HOST-1-IP to refresh the entry.

[Pass condition]
UDP #1 and UDP #2 both use MAC-ADDR1, AND a DUT-originated ARP Request for HOST-1-IP appears after the timeout.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_udp1_wrong_eth_dst — UDP #1 didn't use MAC-ADDR1
• Fail_udp2_wrong_eth_dst — UDP #2 didn't use MAC-ADDR1
• Fail_no_udp1 / Fail_no_udp2 — corresponding UDP missing
• Fail_no_arp_request_after_timeout — DUT did not re-ARP despite timeout passing (timer reset by traffic — wrong)

verdicts.Pass: DUT used learned entry through timeout window AND re-ARPed when timer fired — normal aging-under-load
verdicts.Fail_udp1_wrong_eth_dst: UDP #1 did not use the learned MAC
verdicts.Fail_udp2_wrong_eth_dst: UDP #2 did not use the learned MAC
verdicts.Fail_no_arp_request_after_timeout: DUT did not re-ARP after timeout despite continuous traffic — timer wrongly reset by use
